issue_context.title: Default value not allowed for in x-kubernetes-list-map-keys
issue_context.body:
**What happened**:
I have a CRD which was working fine in 1.17. But it fails with in 1.18.

CRD YAML:
https://github.com/kubedb/apimachinery/blob/ok117/api/crds/kubedb.com_memcacheds.yaml

In 1.18, I get the following error:

```
Error: CustomResourceDefinition.apiextensions.k8s.io "memcacheds.kubedb.com" is invalid: spec.validation.openAPIV3Schema.properties[spec].properties[podTemplate].properties[spec].properties[initContainers].items.properties[ports].items.properties[protocol].default: Required value: this property is in x-kubernetes-list-map-keys, so it must have a default or be a required property
```

Then I tried to add a `default` value for the `protocol` field. But now, I am getting this error in 1.18 .

```
The CustomResourceDefinition "memcacheds.kubedb.com" is invalid: spec.validation.openAPIV3Schema.properties[spec].properties[podTemplate].properties[spec].properties[initContainers].items.properties[ports].items.properties[protocol].default: Forbidden: must not be set
```

I am generating the CRD YAMLs using kubebuilder controller-tools v0.3.0 from this Go source file:

https://github.com/kubedb/apimachinery/blob/f118/apis/kubedb/v1alpha1/memcached_types.go

**What you expected to happen**:
I expected the CRD yaml to work in 1.18 like it did in 1.17 .

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
Just create a cluster using kind and do `kubectl create -f`

**Anything else we need to know?**:

**Environment**:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`): 1.18
- Cloud provider or hardware configuration: kind
- OS (e.g: `cat /etc/os-release`):
- Kernel (e.g. `uname -a`):
- Install tools:
- Network plugin and version (if this is a network-related bug):
- Others:

/kind bug
/sig api-machinery
/area custom-resources
comments:
cc: @sttts 

Can you please help me understand the default value is not acceptable here?

Also, this is using the PodTemplate and Go types from the core/v1 .

Just so you now the example CronJob yaml in controller-tools project also does not work in 1.18 

https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/controller-tools/blob/v0.3.0/pkg/crd/testdata/testdata.kubebuilder.io_cronjobs.yaml

```
$ kubectl version --short
Client Version: v1.18.3
Server Version: v1.18.2

$ kubectl create -f https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/controller-tools/raw/v0.3.0/pkg/crd/testdata/testdata.kubebuilder.io_cronjobs.yaml
The CustomResourceDefinition "cronjobs.testdata.kubebuilder.io" is invalid: 
* spec.validation.openAPIV3Schema.properties[spec].properties[jobTemplate].properties[spec].properties[template].properties[spec].properties[initContainers].items.properties[ports].items.properties[protocol].default: Required value: this property is in x-kubernetes-list-map-keys, so it must have a default or be a required property
* spec.validation.openAPIV3Schema.properties[spec].properties[jobTemplate].properties[spec].properties[template].properties[spec].properties[containers].items.properties[ports].items.properties[protocol].default: Required value: this property is in x-kubernetes-list-map-keys, so it must have a default or be a required property
* spec.validation.openAPIV3Schema.properties[spec].properties[embeddedResource].properties: Required value: must not be empty if x-kubernetes-embedded-resource is true without x-kubernetes-preserve-unknown-fields

```

properties defined as list map keys must either be required or have a default value. Otherwise merge behavior on list-map items that do not specify is undefined. that bug was fixed in 1.18. 

You can specify default attributes using the v1 CRD API. To use list-map keys in a v1beta1 CRD, the properties must be made required (specifying default values is only available in v1 CRDs, see https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/access-kubernetes-api/custom-resources/custom-resource-definitions/#defaulting)
Thanks @liggitt ! What is the best way to keep up with this type of breaking changes for CRDs?

> Thanks @liggitt ! What is the best way to keep up with this type of breaking changes for CRDs?

This was part of the release notes: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/88076

The whole change was unfortunate: `x-kubernetes-list-map-keys´ had been introduced to CRDs earlier, but nobody added the necessary validations for CRDs and CRs. https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/88076 fixed that. On that road we noticed that we need stricter requirements on the map keys to make the mechanism sound.

Thanks, @sttts ! For me the confusing part was that somewhere kubebuilder controller-tools started auto generating `x-kubernetes-list-map-keys` because once I switched from controller-toold v0.2.x to v0.3.0 it started showing up. Should there be an explicit annotation needed for controller-tools to auto generate `x-kubernetes-list-map-keys` ?

On a separate note, should k/api add these default annotations so that CRD authors can use their types? I know this discussion happened with ObjectMeta but here we are talking about any types from k/api.

> For me the confusing part was that somewhere kubebuilder controller-tools started auto generating x-kubernetes-list-map-keys because once I switched from controller-toold v0.2.x to v0.3.0 it started showing up. 

I'd find that surprising as well. 

> Should there be an explicit annotation needed for controller-tools to auto generate x-kubernetes-list-map-keys

I would expect so… list map keys are an explicit decision about the shape of the custom resource API… I'm not sure how controller-tools would automatically infer this.

> On a separate note, should k/api add these default annotations so that CRD authors can use their types?

Indicating default values declaratively makes sense to me, though I wouldn't expect kubebuilder-specific annotations

It seems that the listType annotations were added sometime ago (Oct, 2018) but only recent version of kubebuilder (Dec 2019) started using those when generating CRD YAML.

- https://github.com/kubernetes/api/commit/47160d10e38963082e8d35a474e274debc7cb016
- https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/controller-tools/pull/347

So, the only missing piece is that core types lack any way to indicate default values. I can see why kubebuilder annotations won't make sense here. So, should I file a new feature request for adding an annotation for default values and annotating core types with that?

> So, the only missing piece is that core types lack any way to indicate default values. I can see why kubebuilder annotations won't make sense here. So, should I file a new feature request for adding an annotation for default values and annotating core types with that?

Indicating defaults in struct annotations has been on the backlog for a while (xref https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/25460). Note that not all of our defaults can be expressed declaratively (some defaults vary depending on values of other fields, for example), but as far as I'm aware the ones used as keys in list-map items are constant. A KEP proposing a specific approach would be welcome.
@tamalsaha hey did you make some progress on that issue ?

Another workaround by editing generated CRD with sed:
https://github.com/cybozu-go/coil/blob/6afd89c1cd9261429a9a8ed408a33f144176e57f/v2/Makefile#L30-L33

review_comments: I'm not opposed to adding indicators of default values to kubernetes types, but I would not expect kubebuilder annotations on core types

+1 to what you say here @liggitt, although there is a real problem right now in that:

1) the default value *must* be specified when something is used as a list map key
2) there is no way for kubebuilder to introspect and understand what default value is needed (in the case where it _can_ be defined declaratively)

I notice in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/91395#issuecomment-634029609 you mentioned a KEP to try and resolve this. This may be something I can pick up - presumably this is mostly defining the required/expected annotation (for the simple case where the default _is_ declarative), and potentially "leaving room" for us to express "this default is not simple/declarative".

Is that a correct analysis of the current state? Are you aware of anyone else trying to get this document/plan together?

For some additional context on why this is important to solve, the current "workaround" for this that I have seen either involves either:

1) users running `sed` to fix up their CRDs
2) users forking the k8s.io/api repo (and effectively just applying this patch)
3) users running `sed` to mark the affected fields as `required`

Neither of these is really ideal, and it'd be great to 'nip this' before these sorts of patterns proliferate across the ecosystem

In the meantime, kubebuilder annotations were added to https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/92660

Those are a bit different 1) because we expect those condition types to be reused in many custom resources, and 2) they are all about adding validation, not defining defaulting.

The main things I expect from a "default" annotation:
* it must be valid JSON (kube-builder appears to allow unquoted keys)
* it must be declarative for properties used as keys in a listType=map, because server-side apply will start using those inspected values

As a strawman, `+default=<valid JSON that can be unmarshaled into the field>` seems reasonable
